summary: Pet tab description-alignment fix took 3 attempts: nameRow min-height and descLabel vertical hugging both shipped as fixes in codogotchi-25 but were each independently insufficient.
problem: codogotchi-25 documented a single nameRow min-height fix as resolving description top-alignment, but the user reported it 'still bottom aligned' after that landed. A second attempt pinned descLabel.setContentHuggingPriority(.required, for: .vertical) to stop the label stretching under the equal-height-row constraint added in an earlier phase; this was reported fixed but the user's next round of screenshots showed it only worked for cards that already had a badge-pills row beneath the description — cards with zero badges (rightBottomAnchor = descLabel.bottomAnchor directly, no pillsRow intermediary) still misaligned. A third, separate symptom surfaced in the same screenshots: cards that DID have a pill showed it floating immediately under a short description instead of sitting at the card's bottom, because pillsRow.topAnchor was pinned to descLabel.bottomAnchor with a fixed (==) 6pt offset rather than a flexible minimum.
solution: Replaced the conditional pillsRow (only created `if !entryBadges.isEmpty`) with an always-present pillsRow (zero height when there are no badges), so every card's right-column bottom anchor is the same anchor type. Changed pillsRow.topAnchor from `equalTo` to `greaterThanOrEqualTo` descLabel.bottomAnchor, so any extra height forced by the row's equal-height-to-tallest-sibling constraint opens up as slack between the description and the pills row rather than stretching the description (already prevented by the prior hugging-priority fix) or leaving the pills row stranded near the top. The existing leftBottom/rightBottom/preferRight triad now always resolves against pillsRow.bottomAnchor, which bottom-anchors pills consistently regardless of badge count.

fixCommit.subject: fix(menubar): always render badge pills row, bottom-anchored, so description and pills align consistently

reachability.evidence: Each of the 3 rounds required a running app screenshot to detect: round 1 (nameRow height parity) looked plausible in the diff and built clean; round 2 (descLabel hugging) also built clean and matched the stated root-cause theory but the user's screenshot evidence (cards with vs without a pill behaving differently) was the only thing that exposed the remaining gap; round 3 additionally surfaced a second, previously-undiagnosed symptom (pills not bottom-anchored) visible only by comparing a short-description card with a pill against the rest of the grid.
reachability.promptLesson: In a content-hugging Auto Layout chain forced taller by a sibling equal-height constraint, EVERY required-priority leaf in the chain needs to either be the designated 'flex absorber' (a `>=` gap) or have hugging explicitly pinned — fixing only one stretchy leaf (descLabel) without auditing the rest of the chain (the descLabel-to-pillsRow gap was still a fixed `==`) leaves the next leaf in the chain as the de facto, unintended absorber, which manifests as a *different* visual symptom (pills positioned wrong) rather than a re-occurrence of the original one. When equalizing heights forces slack into a layout, explicitly name which single gap is the flex absorber and verify the rest of the chain is fully rigid (required hugging or fixed-size children) end to end, not leaf by leaf as bugs are reported.

testReachability: Not unit-reachable — pure Auto Layout geometry only observable by rendering the Settings > Pet tab grid with a mix of badge-having and badge-less pets and visually comparing description start position and pill bottom position across cards. No snapshot/layout test exists for this view.

summary: The P8.05 lockstep 'Hooks are out of date — click Update' banner fired on any bundled-vs-installed CLI version difference, so a pure binary-internals bump with byte-identical hook registration (e.g. the 1.0.0->1.0.1 hook-binary bump) nagged the user to re-register hooks that were already correct.
problem: LockstepPolicy.needsUpdate returned `bundledVersion != installedVersion` and, via GeneralTabViewModel.shouldShowUpdateBanner, drove the actionable Update-hooks banner. The version string was doing double duty: it stood in for BOTH 'the registered command path/event slots changed' (genuine registration drift, where Update is required) AND 'only the binary's internal behavior changed' (same command path, same event slots, new binary auto-delivered at the same Resources/ path — where Update rewrites byte-identical config). hooks status already exposed the true registration signal (installed = every expected event wired; partially_installed = some wired) but those use a LOOSE isCodogotchiCommand token match, so they could not see command-path format drift (bare name vs absolute bundle path) and the banner reached past them to the weaker version proxy. Commit c52a5bb0 (canonicalize active-session.json write target) and 8f74fc4e (1.0.0->1.0.1 bump) are concrete internals-only bumps that would fire a false 'out of date' prompt on the next app release.
solution: Added a per-platform registration_current boolean to `codogotchi hooks status --json` (packages/cli/src/hooks.ts): claudeRegistrationCurrent/codexRegistrationCurrent verify every expected event carries the EXACT hook command the running binary would write now (shellQuoteIfNeeded(resolveHookCommand(process.execPath))), not merely a loose codogotchi-hook token; Cursor/VS Code/Antigravity invoke the bare command name so theirs equals full-wiring. The CODOGOTCHI_HOME env prefix is deliberately excluded from the fingerprint because it is caller-supplied (getCodogotchiHome) and cannot be reliably reconstructed. Swift: HooksStatusSnapshot.Platform gains registrationCurrent (defaults true so stale caches never false-alarm); GeneralTabViewModel replaces the version-driven banner trigger with hasStaleRegistration (present-but-not-current, subsuming the old partially-installed-only check). shouldShowUpdateBanner = hasStaleRegistration || hasUnhookedDetectedPlatform. A version-only bump is now silent; the binary version stays visible in the About tab. needsBannerUpdate (the version predicate) is retained for diagnostics but no longer wired to the banner.

fixCommit.subject: fix(menubar): key Update-hooks banner on registration fingerprint, not version

reachability.evidence: The conflation is visible in the P8.05 diff itself: LockstepPolicy.needsUpdate returns `bundledVersion != installedVersion` and its consumer renders 'Hooks are out of date — click Update to apply the bundled version.' The stronger, truthful signal (registration wiring) already existed in the same subsystem — hooks status computed installed/partially_installed per platform. A reviewer comparing the banner's trigger against the signals hooks status already exposed had enough evidence at review time to ask whether a version-string inequality is the right gate for a 'your hooks are broken, re-register now' CTA.
reachability.promptLesson: When a user-facing CTA that claims something is broken/out-of-date is gated on a PROXY signal (a version-string comparison, a timestamp, a build id), ask whether the proxy can diverge from the actual condition it stands for, and whether the real condition is already computable from state the system holds. Here 'hooks out of date' really means 'the installed registration differs from what we would write now' — a fingerprint the CLI could compute directly — while the version string also moves on internals-only bumps that change nothing on disk. Attack surface for review: for any 'X is stale/out of date → prompt user to fix' banner, demand that X be the narrowest true predicate for the fix the button performs, not a broader proxy that triggers no-op actions.

testReachability: Fully reachable once registration_current exists. CLI: 3 new hooks.test.ts cases (fresh install -> current; installed-but-drifted command path with `installed` still true -> not current; missing event slot -> not current) plus a router-hooks.test.ts --json shape assertion; 47/47 pass. Swift: testNoBannerWhenVersionDiffersButRegistrationCurrent is the direct regression for the 1.0.1 case (version differs, registration current -> no banner), plus stale/partial cases; 27/27 pass. The ORIGINAL gap was untested because the lockstep tests only asserted the version predicate (needsUpdate/needsBannerUpdate) in isolation and never asserted that a version bump with unchanged registration should NOT surface the banner — the missing assertion was the same shape as the missing behavior.

summary: With Session Pets disabled, switching a platform Own/Minimalist <-> Combined left the old window undismissed in both directions: Own/Minimalist -> Combined never tore down the stale directly-keyed window, and Combined -> Own/Minimalist could nondeterministically leave the shared "combined" window stuck on a same-tick timestamp tie.
problem: P15.03 (resolveRenderKeys) moved combined-mode folding upstream of the pool: a combined-mode origin's sessions are now pre-folded to the literal "combined" key before FloatingPetWindowPool ever sees the snapshot. Two teardown paths still assumed the pre-P15.03 shape where the pool itself did the folding. (1) Step 6a looked for the origin's own key inside the snapshot's combinedKeys to decide what to tear down on Own/Minimalist -> Combined; with pre-folded input that key never reappears, so the loop body never ran and the stale own/minimalist window lingered until idle-dismiss TTL (default 300s, or forever if TTL is Never). (2) Step 8's else-branch (dismiss "combined" when no combined-folded keys remain, i.e. Combined -> Own/Minimalist) gated the dismissal on last-active immunity unconditionally, even when zero origins are combined-mode anymore. When the user toggles the mode picker without any new agent activity in between, the freshly-added directly-keyed render key can carry the exact same updated_at as the stale "combined" entry already tracked in lastUpdatedAt; Swift's max(by:) tie-break there is Dictionary-iteration-order dependent, so "combined" could nondeterministically win last-active election and never be dismissed. Verified flaky against the pre-fix code (2 of 3 repeated runs failed on a same-timestamp regression test) confirming this is a genuine latent bug, not a one-off.
solution: Step 6a (apps/menubar/Sources/FloatingPetWindowPool.swift) now derives its collapse set from the pool's own open `windows` keys filtered by `windowKey(for:) == "combined"` under the CURRENT customization, instead of scanning the snapshot's combinedKeys -- this works whether the driver feeds pre-folded or legacy unfolded input, and also covers session-keyed windows. Step 8's else-branch now branches on `combinedModeOrigins()` (read fresh from customization, independent of this tick's snapshot): if no origin is combined-mode anymore, dismiss "combined" unconditionally (mirroring Step 5a's off-mode dismissal, bypassing last-active immunity); if at least one origin is still combined-mode but simply absent from this tick's snapshot (a transient polling gap), keep the existing TTL/last-active protection so a single gapped tick doesn't flash the window off. Added 4 regression tests exercising the pre-folded resolver->pool seam directly (via resolveRenderKeys, not hand-built render keys) for both mode-switch directions, two of them with tied timestamps to pin the nondeterministic tie-break. Full mac suite: 815/815 pass.

fixCommit.subject: fix(phase-15-qc): dismiss stale window on any transition away from combined mode

reachability.evidence: Both symptoms are only observable by running the app and manually toggling a platform's mode picker between Own/Minimalist and Combined -- no unit test caught either because the existing pool test suite fed the legacy unfolded per-origin shape rather than the pre-folded output resolveRenderKeys has produced since P15.03 (the Step 6 code comment says as much: "the pre-P15.03 shape the existing tests feed"). The second symptom (Combined -> Own/Minimalist tie-break) additionally required a same-tick timestamp coincidence to surface, which only shows up in live dogfooding where a developer flips a setting without triggering new agent activity in between -- a scenario no automated test exercised.

testReachability: Not caught by the original phase-15 test suite because tests fed the resolver's pre-P15.03 unfolded shape. Now covered: testOwnToCombinedCollapsesPreviousWindowWithPreFoldedSnapshot, testMinimalistToCombinedCollapsesPreviousWindowWithPreFoldedSnapshot, testCombinedToOwnDismissesCombinedEvenOnTimestampTie, testCombinedToMinimalistDismissesCombinedEvenOnTimestampTie -- all four route through resolveRenderKeys via makeResolvedSnapshot rather than hand-built render keys, and the last two use tied updated_at timestamps to pin the nondeterministic election bug deterministically.

summary: Toggling Session Pets on/off for an Own/Minimalist-mode origin did not dismiss the now-stale window in either direction: enabling left the old plain-origin window running alongside new session windows, and disabling left the old session-keyed windows running alongside the new plain-origin window.
problem: sessionPetsEnabled is read only in RenderKeyResolver.swift:69 to decide render-key SHAPE (plain origin vs origin:session_id per session) -- completely independent of PlatformMode. None of FloatingPetWindowPool's existing teardown branches keyed off this toggle: off-mode teardown (Step 5a) only fires on mode == .off; TTL/last-active immunity protects the sole or most-recently-updated window indefinitely if the origin has no rival key; the codogotchi-28 combined-mode collapse (Step 6a) only fires when windowKey(for:) resolves to "combined"; and the mode-mismatch collapse (Step 6b) only re-checks a render key that is still present in this tick's snapshot under the SAME key string -- but toggling session-pets makes the key disappear and reappear under a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT string (plain "claude_code" vs "claude_code:sess-1"), so no existing branch's precondition is ever met in either direction. This is the third distinct trigger, after codogotchi-06 (a new PlatformMode enum case added in P14) and codogotchi-28 (an upstream data-shape refactor moving combined-mode folding, this same P15 QC session), producing the identical symptom in this exact file: a stale window from before an identity-changing customization edit is never torn down because teardown is a set of reactive, transition-specific branches rather than a rule derived from current state.
solution: Added Step 6a2 to FloatingPetWindowPool.update() (apps/menubar/Sources/FloatingPetWindowPool.swift): for every open window key other than "combined", compare its SHAPE (plain origin vs session-keyed, via isSessionKeyed) against its origin's current sessionPetsEnabled setting; a mismatch is torn down unconditionally, bypassing TTL/last-active immunity, mirroring how Step 5a already bypasses that immunity for off-mode. Combined-mode origins are excluded from this check since combined folds unconditionally regardless of sessionPetsEnabled (already owned by the codogotchi-28 fix) and are never plain/session-keyed to begin with. Added two regression tests -- testEnablingSessionPetsDismissesPlainOriginWindow and testDisablingSessionPetsDismissesSessionKeyedWindows -- both confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code (5 assertion failures total) and pass deterministically post-fix. Full mac suite: 817/817 pass.

fixCommit.subject: fix(phase-15-qc): dismiss stale window on Session Pets toggle in either direction

reachability.evidence: Only observable by running the app and manually toggling Session Pets for a platform between off and on while a window is open -- no unit test caught it because the existing pool test suite never exercised the sessionPetsEnabled dimension of a mode-preserving customization change; every prior test that changed customization mid-run varied platformModes, never sessionPetsEnabled alone.

testReachability: Now covered by testEnablingSessionPetsDismissesPlainOriginWindow and testDisablingSessionPetsDismissesSessionKeyedWindows, both routing through resolveRenderKeys via makeResolvedSnapshot for the real resolver-pool seam.

summary: The menubar dropdown's "Hide/Show <X> Pet" items for session-keyed windows title-cased the raw "origin:session_id" window key, surfacing the literal session UUID to the user instead of a friendly session label or ordinal.
problem: MenubarMenu.displayName(for:) (apps/menubar/Sources/MenubarMenu.swift) is a pure platform-name switch over the window key ("claude_code" -> "Claude Code", etc.) with a default case of `key.replacingOccurrences(of: "_", with: " ").capitalized`. Phase 15 introduced session-keyed window keys ("origin:session_id") flowing through the same `activeOrigins`/`hiddenWindowKeys` arrays that already fed this function's call sites in buildPetSection(in:), but displayName itself was never updated to recognize the new key shape: an unrecognized session-keyed key fell straight through to the default case, title-casing the entire "origin:uuid" string and rendering the raw session UUID verbatim in a "Hide Claude Code:B116CB55-... Pet" menu item. The plumbing to avoid this already existed and was already wired to the per-window session badge/tooltip (FloatingPetWindowPool.sessionLabel(forWindowKey:) reading SessionLabelStore's custom rename, and .sessionNumber(forWindowKey:) reading SessionNumberAllocator's per-origin ordinal, both added in earlier phase-15 tickets and wired into FloatingPetController by commit d99a7e19) -- but no ticket in the phase-15 decomposition scoped the menubar dropdown item title as a consumer of the session-keyed window-key shape, so it was never touched to read from that same source of truth. The gap was not visible in any single ticket's diff: the session-labeling plumbing landed in FloatingPetWindowPool/FloatingPetController/SessionLabelStore, while the affected code lives in the unrelated MenubarMenu.swift, so a reviewer of any one ticket's diff would not have had the other file in view to connect the two.
solution: Split MenubarMenu.displayName(for:) into platformDisplayName(for:) (the original pure origin/platform-name switch, now called with the origin substring) and a new displayName(for: key:), marked @MainActor to call the pool. For a session-keyed key, displayName keeps the platform prefix (origin(forWindowKey:) before the colon) and appends ":<label>" using pool.sessionLabel(forWindowKey:) if a custom rename is set, else ":Session <n>" from pool.sessionNumber(forWindowKey:); plain-origin keys (session pets off for that platform) fall through unchanged to platformDisplayName. Added two regression tests in MenuItemsTests.swift (testSessionKeyedOriginFallsBackToSessionNumberWhenNoLabelIsSet, testSessionKeyedOriginPrefersCustomSessionLabelOverSessionNumber) exercising a real session-keyed window key with injected renderKeyIdentities and a stub sessionLabelReader. Full mac suite: 819/819 pass. Manually verified against the running app by the developer, who confirmed the dropdown now shows the session label/ordinal instead of the raw UUID.

fixCommit.subject: fix(phase-15-qc): label session-keyed menubar pet items with session name, not raw UUID

reachability.evidence: Only observable by opening the live running app's menubar dropdown with 2+ active session-keyed platforms -- the developer caught it via a screenshot of the actual dropdown showing raw UUIDs. No unit test in the phase-15 suite exercised MenuItemsTests with a session-keyed window key at all (all prior fixtures used plain origins like "claude_code"/"cursor"), and the session-labeling plumbing (SessionLabelStore, SessionNumberAllocator) lives in files separate from MenubarMenu.swift, so no single ticket's diff put both the new key shape and this old display function in the same review surface.

testReachability: Now covered by testSessionKeyedOriginFallsBackToSessionNumberWhenNoLabelIsSet and testSessionKeyedOriginPrefersCustomSessionLabelOverSessionNumber, both constructing a real session-keyed render key via renderKeyIdentities and asserting the rendered menu item title.

summary: Clicking Focus or the X (dismiss) affordance on a session-keyed AttentionBubble only acted on the clicked session, leaving sibling sessions' bubbles for the same platform still showing — even though Focus can only foreground the platform app as a whole, not the specific thread that needed attention.
problem: AttentionBubbleView.performAction() (Focus) and dismissBubble() (X) both funnel into the same onDismiss closure, which MenubarApp.swift wired per session-keyed window to StateJsonWriter.dismissAttention(at:origin:sessionId:) — the P15.04 session-precise variant that rewrites exactly one origin:sessionId.json slice. That narrowing was correct for Force Idle/dismiss-by-the-owning-session, but Focus predates session-pets fan-out (ticket-02, phase-06) and was never revisited when ticket-04 (phase-15) introduced one window per active session for the same origin. AppKit's NSWorkspace.runningApplications.activate() can only foreground an app bundle, never a specific window/thread inside it, so once the user clicks Focus they are about to see every thread of that platform anyway — but every sibling session's bubble kept showing (and its state.d slice kept carrying `attention`), reappearing on the very next poll tick even for the one the user just clicked, and never getting cleared for the untouched siblings.
solution: Added StateJsonWriter.dismissAllSessionsAttention(at:origin:) (apps/menubar/Sources/StateJsonWriter.swift), which scans state.d/ via StateJsonReader.parseSliceFilename and idles every session slice matching the origin (not just the winner or the exact clicked session). Added FloatingPetWindowPool.clearAttentionBubbles(sharingOriginWith:) (apps/menubar/Sources/FloatingPetWindowPool.swift), which iterates the pool's open windows and calls applyAttention(nil, nil) on every window sharing the clicked window's owning origin, so sibling bubbles hide immediately instead of waiting a poll tick. Rewired both onAttentionDismissed closures in MenubarApp.swift (own-mode and minimalist factories) to call these two together instead of the single-session-precise path whenever FloatingPetWindowPool.sessionIdentity(forWindowKey:) resolves (i.e. session pets are on for that origin); the plain-origin/combined branch is unchanged. Added testClearAttentionBubblesHidesEverySessionWindowSharingTheOrigin (FloatingPetWindowPoolTests.swift) and three StateJsonWriterTests (clears every session not just the winner, leaves other origins untouched, skips stale-mtime slices). Full mac suite: 823/823 pass. Developer manually verified against the running app with two concurrent sessions on the same platform.

fixCommit.subject: fix(phase-15-qc): dismiss all sibling session bubbles on Focus/X for a platform

reachability.evidence: Only observable by running the app with session pets enabled and two or more concurrent sessions open for the same platform, then clicking Focus or X on one session's bubble and watching whether the sibling session's bubble also clears — no unit test exercised the Focus/dismiss action against a multi-session-per-origin pool state, since the existing FloatingPetWindowPoolTests and StateJsonWriterTests coverage for dismiss/forceIdle was written to prove session-precision (touch only the clicked session), the opposite property this fix required for Focus.

summary: With a per-origin session cap set, when the cap evicts a non-active (idle/errored/waiting) session's window to make room, the newly-promoted active session that takes over the freed slot spawned at the default floating-pet position instead of the evicted pet's exact location and size.
problem: Ticket-07 (P15.07, SessionSelectionPolicy) introduced per-origin session-cap eviction/promotion: a non-active session drops to `pending` (its window torn down) and an active session is promoted into the freed rendered slot. Neither ticket-07 nor the phase-15 product plan says anything about what on-screen position the newly-promoted session's window should take — the ticket's Review Focus section covers the eviction-rank partition, TTL, and pruning, but never the frame/position dimension of a slot changing hands. FloatingPetWindowPool's spawn path (Step 7 of update()) treats every newly-spawned session window uniformly regardless of why it is spawning: it always resolves position via the window factory's `AppStateStore.loadFrame(for: <brand-new session id>, ...)`, which has never seen that session id before and falls through to `FloatingFramePolicy.defaultFrame`. This is a genuine tie-break the ticket left unresolved between two valid designs (each session keeps its own independent slot vs. a promoted session takes over the vacated slot) — not a self-evident invariant either builder would land on the same way by instinct, since every other spawn path in the same function (a brand-new origin, a brand-new session with no cap pressure) legitimately DOES use the default-frame path, so there was no existing precedent flagging the cap-eviction case as special.
solution: Added `currentFrame: CGRect { get }` and `func adoptFrame(_ frame: CGRect)` to `FloatingPetWindowControlling` (apps/menubar/Sources/FloatingPetController.swift), with a `.zero`/no-op default extension for stubs that do not need it. Implemented both on `FloatingPetController` and `MinimalistWindowController`, reusing each controller's existing `saveClampedFrame` persistence path so the inherited frame is both shown immediately and saved to `AppStateStore` (so a relaunch keeps the same slot). In `FloatingPetWindowPool.update()` (apps/menubar/Sources/FloatingPetWindowPool.swift), added `evictedSessionFrames: [String: CGRect]`, a per-origin one-shot cache: Step 6c now captures a session's `currentFrame` the instant `SessionSelectionPolicy.select` moves it from rendered to `pending` (before Step 7 tears the window down), and Step 7's spawn branch consumes (and removes) that entry via `adoptFrame` the next time a new window spawns for that same origin — so only the very next promoted sibling inherits the freed slot, not some later unrelated spawn. Added `testEvictedSessionFrameIsInheritedByTheIncomingActiveSession` and `testInheritedFrameDoesNotLeakToAnUnrelatedOrigin` (FloatingPetWindowPoolTests.swift) plus `testAdoptFrameMovesPanelAndPersistsTheInheritedFrame` (FloatingPetControllerTests.swift). Full mac suite: 826/826 pass. Developer manually verified against the running app by forcing a session-cap eviction and confirming the promoted pet appeared exactly where the evicted one had been.

fixCommit.subject: fix(phase-15-qc): inherit evicted session's frame for the incoming active session

reachability.evidence: Ticket-07's spec, Review Focus section, and the phase-15 product plan never mention window position/frame handling for session-cap eviction or promotion — only the eviction-rank partition, TTL, and manual prune are specified. A competent builder implementing exactly the specified partition logic would have shipped the observed behavior (default position on every spawn) without any signal to stop and ask, since every other spawn path in the same function legitimately uses the default-frame path too; nothing in the diff or ticket made the cap-eviction case look special enough to flag in review.

summary: Right-clicking Force Idle on a pet rewrote only the state.d/ activity slice, leaving that window's SOA ticket/gate badge and P15.08 conflict speech bubble on screen since both are driven by separate .gate.json/.context.json polling state the idle rewrite never touched.
problem: Force Idle (apps/menubar/Sources/MenubarApp.swift, wired to StateJsonWriter.forceIdle) predates both the ticket/gate badge (GateBadgePanel, pre-phase-14) and the P15.08 conflict SpeechBubblePanel. Its own doc comment frames it as "rewrite this pet's displayed slice back to idle so a stuck ... animation clears" -- scoped to the activity animation only. Neither newer UI element was revisited when it landed: the badge is resolved each ~1s poll tick from resolveGateBadgeContent(deliveryContext:, sourceEvent:) against .context.json's own owner/status/lease-expiry fields (GateJsonReader.swift), and the conflict bubble similarly from a separate payload -- both entirely independent of the state.d/ activity_state field Force Idle actually writes. A user right-clicking Force Idle on a visibly stuck pet reasonably expects every stuck-state indicator on that pet to clear, not just the sprite animation.
solution: Both onForceIdle closures in MenubarApp.swift (Own-mode and Minimalist-mode window factories) now also call panel.applyGateBadge(content: nil) and panel.applyConflictBubble(nil) on the targeted window, weakly capturing panel to avoid a retain cycle, alongside the existing StateJsonWriter.forceIdle call. Scoped to the exact window Force Idle was invoked on (not fanned out to sibling sessions), matching how Force Idle's state.d/ write is already session-precise. applyGateBadge/applyConflictBubble were pre-existing, already-tested methods (also used by hide()); this only adds two call sites. Full mac suite: 840/840 pass. Developer manually verified against the running app after also discovering and clearing an unrelated stale local test fixture (a leftover .gate.json/.context.json pair with a same-day lease) that was independently bleeding a stale badge onto the live pet via the origin-scoped (not session-scoped) badge design -- confirmed as pre-existing, intentional origin-level scoping (see LivePollingDriver.swift's resolveRenderedPlatforms doc comment) and explicitly left untouched, not folded into this fix.

fixCommit.subject: fix(phase-15-qc): clear SOA badges and conflict bubble on Force Idle

reachability.evidence: Only observable by running the app, getting a pet into a state with a visible ticket/gate badge or conflict bubble, and right-clicking Force Idle to watch whether they clear -- no automated test exercised onForceIdle's badge/bubble interaction, since the wiring lives in private MenubarApp.swift closures outside the FloatingPetControllerTests/MinimalistPanelController surface that tests applyGateBadge/applyConflictBubble directly but never through Force Idle.

testReachability: Not covered by an automated regression test -- the onForceIdle wiring is inside MenubarApp.swift's private window-factory closures, which the existing test suite does not exercise (no MenubarApp-level integration test harness exists for this wiring layer, matching the pattern already noted for the sibling dismissAttention/clearAttentionBubbles wiring). Verified via full mac suite (840/840, no regressions) plus manual developer verification in the running app.

summary: The phase-15 product plan and tickets never addressed what happens to an already-active platform pet at the instant session-pets is toggled on for that platform: the incumbent pet should be grandfathered in as "Session 1" (keeping its custom label if any), and every other live sibling session should stay hidden until it shows activity after that toggle instant, re-arming on every subsequent off->on toggle.
problem: implementation-plan.md's walkthrough only narrates enabling session-pets and THEN starting fresh concurrent sessions ("enables session pets for a platform... runs three concurrent agent sessions... watches three pet panels appear labeled Session 1/2/3") — it never considers the case where a session is already rendering as the collapsed single pet at the moment of the toggle. Ticket-01 (contracts-session-pets-fields) only specifies the raw sessionPetsEnabled/sessionCap fields, with no mention of toggle-time continuity. As shipped by ticket-04 (pool-per-session-fanout), toggling session-pets on fanned out a real window for EVERY live state.d/ session for that origin simultaneously, discarding the continuity of whichever single pet the user was already looking at and surfacing every other live session (including long-idle ones) at once. This is a plausible reading of the spec text ("Own/Minimalist with session-pets on keep each origin:session_id key" carves out no exception), but not the behavior the developer actually wanted, and it is a genuine tie-break the ticket left unresolved between two valid designs — not a self-evident invariant either builder lands on the same way by instinct.
solution: Grilled the request into 4 concrete decisions before writing any code: (1) grandfather = the current winner (freshest updated_at) at the instant of toggle, or none if no live session exists; (2) the "Session 1" slot is not permanently pinned — once that session ages out/prunes, numbering reverts to normal allocation; (3) sibling admission = any state.d write with updated_at strictly after the activation timestamp; (4) persist BOTH the activation timestamp and the exact grandfathered session_id (not just the timestamp) so an idle grandfather survives an app relaunch. Implemented via two new CustomizationSnapshot fields (sessionPetsActivatedAt, sessionPetsGrandfatheredSessionId, defaulting to absent/no-gate for pre-existing data so already-enabled origins are unaffected), a CustomizationTabViewModel.setSessionPetsEnabled off->on branch that snapshots the current winner and carries over any existing plain-origin custom label, and a RenderKeyResolver admission gate that excludes any non-grandfathered session whose activity does not postdate the toggle. Landed in 42a81dbe. Because this went through ad-hoc QC delivery rather than the SoA phase-execution path, a dedicated /code-review pass (8 finder angles + 1-vote verify) ran on the diff before any manual testing and caught 3 correctness bugs in this new code: the activation timestamp used whole-second ISO8601 precision, letting a sibling that wrote just before the real toggle instant slip past the strict `>` gate within the same wall-clock second; the grandfather winner-selection used max(by:) over an unsorted Dictionary, resolving an exact updated_at tie nondeterministically instead of matching RenderKeyResolver's own sorted-iteration tie-break convention; and the label carryover unconditionally clobbered a label already set directly at the destination session key.
